main_text.p: conditores. Frequéter etiam Iuris auctores in Pãdectis appellantur: ut apud Vlp. ex Diuorum fratrum rescripto in L.17. D. de iur. patron. Et Proculum sanè, non leuem Iuris auctorē, in hac opinione fuisse. Item paulo pòst: Plurium etiam Iuris auctorum, sed & Saluij Iuliani, amici nostri, clarissimi uiri, hanc sententiam fuisse. Martianus item ex rescripto Diui Pij, an mora facta intelligatur, neque constitutione ulla, neq; Iuris auctorum quæstione decidi posse. Sic Aggenus Vrbicus. at Cassius Longinus, uir prudentissimus: Iuris auctor hoc statuit,

page.notes: Printed quotation marks («) stand at the line ends down the right edge of the column; they are not text and are not transcribed. Handwritten ink marks in the right margin are not printed and are left out. Long s has been read as plain s in "fuisse", "nostri", "constitutione", "Cassius". Hyphens at line ends are printed as "Pä-" etc.; "Pro-culum" was printed across a line end without a hyphen and is written whole as "Proculum". Mark "aucto-rum" has an irregular letter form, read as "auctorum".
